name: Collin Brown
title: Workplace Operations Manager
one_liner: Workplace Operations professional with 7+ years building scalable systems, optimizing vendor performance, and leading office environments across high-growth companies.
bio: I manage the full lifecycle of office environments — from construction build-outs and vendor negotiations to employee experience programming and internal communications. I'm known for building scalable systems, optimizing vendor performance, and using operational data to improve workplace strategy, reduce costs, and enhance in-office engagement. Currently leading the multi-floor renovation of Rho's SF headquarters at 325 Pacific Ave, coordinating 15+ vendors across electrical, flooring, HVAC, AV, and millwork.

skill_descriptions.Workplace Operations: Workplace operations is the core of my practice — managing the systems, spaces, and logistics that keep an office running reliably. I approach it broadly rather than as a narrow function, which means I'm comfortable owning both tactical execution and the strategic setup that makes scale possible.
skill_descriptions.Facilities Management: I've managed facilities across multi-floor commercial build-outs, coworking environments, and corporate offices — handling vendor coordination, building liaison work, and the physical environment end-to-end. My focus is on operational reliability: making sure the space doesn't become a distraction for the people working in it.
skill_descriptions.Vendor Coordination: Vendor management is where I tend to have the most direct financial and operational impact. I handle the full lifecycle — sourcing, negotiating, onboarding, compliance, and accountability — and I've developed a strong instinct for identifying when a vendor relationship isn't delivering.
skill_descriptions.Budget Management: I track and audit budgets as a core part of the role, not an afterthought. I've caught billing discrepancies, identified savings opportunities, and delivered design initiatives under budget by being deliberate about spend from day one rather than reconciling at the end.
skill_descriptions.Space Planning: Space planning is one of the more creative parts of my work — translating headcount, workflow, and culture into a physical layout. I've applied this at the scale of full multi-floor redesigns and smaller tactical reconfigurations, always working to make the space serve the people using it.
skill_descriptions.Workplace Analytics: I use data — primarily occupancy and utilization metrics from tools like Envoy — to make space and programming decisions that are evidence-based rather than intuition-based. This shifts conversations from opinion to observation and makes it easier to measure what's actually working.
skill_descriptions.Employee Experience: Employee experience shapes how I think about almost everything in a workplace: what does it feel like to work here, and what can operations do to improve that? I've built programs, events, and systems specifically aimed at improving how people feel about coming into the office and staying engaged once they're there.
skill_descriptions.Event Programming: I plan and execute workplace events ranging from team happy hours and cultural activations to wellness initiatives and surprise-and-delight moments. My focus is on events that have a clear purpose — building community, signaling care, or reinforcing culture — rather than just filling a calendar.
skill_descriptions.AV/IT Systems: I've managed AV and workplace technology systems across multiple sites, including meeting room AV, digital signage, and shared infrastructure. I'm not an IT specialist, but I'm comfortable owning these systems operationally and working closely with IT partners when deeper technical work is required.
skill_descriptions.Hardware Provisioning: Hardware provisioning has been a consistent part of my onboarding and offboarding responsibilities — making sure people have what they need on Day 1 and that equipment is properly collected, documented, and processed when someone leaves.
skill_descriptions.Process Documentation: I build playbooks and documentation as a natural output of the work, not a separate project. The goal is always the same: reduce dependency on institutional knowledge living in one person's head and make it possible for someone else to run the same process faster next time.
skill_descriptions.Stakeholder Management: Working across departments and leadership levels is a constant in this type of role. I'm comfortable managing up, across, and laterally — whether that's aligning executives on a construction timeline, coordinating between IT and People Ops on an onboarding process, or pushing back on a vendor decision that doesn't serve the project.
